$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: A Pass Not in the Ledger

goal.text: Climb the Cairnstep and see if it belongs on the map.

steps.label: Climb the cairns to the notch
Compare the old and new drawings

plate.narration: Stacked stone cairns climb a narrow notch between snowy peaks. Wind combs the ridges. Far above, griffin aeries cling to the cliffs like nests on a shelf.

cairns.narration: Stone cairns climb a slope toward a notch in the Frostfang Peaks, each one taller than the last. At the lowest cairn, a griffin keeper called Brask sits with a heavy pass ledger open on a flat rock and a pencil behind his ear. "This path was not in my ledger last season. We checked. Is it a real pass, or a trick of the snow?" He peers at you. "Tonight you climb the Cairnstep, and tell me if it belongs on the map."

choices.label: Follow Brask up the cairns

steps.narration: The cairns climb in steps, and the steps are old snow over loose stone. Brask goes ahead, flapping when the slope gets steep. "Touch every cairn as you pass," he calls back. "It is polite, and it helps you balance." How will you climb?

choices.label: Climb in a line, touching each cairn
Scout your own way up the loose slope
Use leap to bound over the loose stretch
Use rally to keep tired legs climbing

climb_line.prompt: Everyone climb the cairn stairs together, one hand on the stones.
climb_line.narration: You walk in a line, and each of you puts a hand on a cairn as you pass. Some cairns wobble. Some go crunch. One is so neat that you want to give it a medal.

onSuccess.narration: Cairn by cairn, you reach the top in a happy line. Not one stone falls.

onFailure.narration: A cairn topples and bounces down the slope, taking a bootful of snow with it. You finish the climb with scraped hands.

climb_scout.prompt: The surest feet pick the way up the loose slope, and the others follow.
climb_scout.narration: Between the cairns, the slope is loose and tricky. The surest feet go first, testing each step. The others follow in the same footprints, like ducklings.

onSuccess.narration: The route holds, step by step. You come up at the notch without a slip.

onFailure.narration: The first route ends at a drop, so you back out and take a longer curve. You reach the notch tired.

climb_leap.prompt: Use leap to bound over the loose stretch with a rope. The hero with leap helps; choose who leads.
climb_leap.narration: A manticore can bound over a loose stretch of slope and tie a rope to the next cairn. The rest of the party climbs up the rope.

onSuccess.narration: One bound, and a rope hangs from the next cairn. The rest of you climb it like a staircase.

onFailure.narration: The bound lands short, but the rope still reaches. You climb it with wobbly knees.

climb_rally.prompt: Use rally to keep tired legs climbing. The songkeeper helps; choose who leads.
climb_rally.narration: A songkeeper can lift a friend who is down. The slope is steep, and the song is a bouncy one, with a different beat for every cairn.

onSuccess.narration: A quick climbing song, and legs that wanted to stop remember how to go.

onFailure.narration: The song is cheerful, but the slope is steep. You reach the top puffing.

notch.narration: You reach the notch, and the wind finds you at once. It combs the ridges on both sides, and it combs your ears too. The whole pass lies below you, a ribbon of stones between two white shoulders. Far off in the sky floats a distant island, small as a loaf in a pond. Brask raises a flag on a stick, and after a moment a tiny flag answers from the island. "Our neighbors," he says. "They watch the weather. We watch the stones."

choices.label: Look at the ledger

ledger.narration: Brask sets his heavy pass ledger on a flat rock and flips it open. Two drawings sit side by side. Last season's shows an unbroken ridge, with no gap in it at all. This season's shows the notch you are standing in. Below both, a pencil line marks the herders' grazing route, cut by water in three places. "One of these drawings is wrong," says Brask. "Compare them, please."

choices.label: Compare the old drawing with the real ridge
Lay the herders' route over the new drawing
Use skyward or glide to read both pages from above

ridge.narration: You stand where Brask made his old drawing and hold the page up against the real mountain. The cairns line up. The ridge does not. A whole section of stone has stepped sideways, like a person in a crowded room. "We can argue about the ink," says Brask, "but the mountain is harder to argue with. Find me exactly where it moved."

choices.label: Match the page to the mountain

ridge_spot.prompt: The sharpest eyes match the drawing to the ridge, line by line, and call out where they stop agreeing.

onSuccess.narration: There! A step in the rock, where the drawing says smooth. You call it out, and Brask makes a neat pencil mark.

onFailure.narration: The lines blur together in the glare. Brask points out the step himself, with a wink. "Snow is hard on eyes," he says.

supplies.narration: You lay the herders' grazing route over the new drawing. Water cut the old route in three places. The new path runs above all three cuts, along a high shelf of dry ground. "So the herd could use it," says Brask, "if the shelf is real. Show me where it joins the cairns."

choices.label: Trace where the shelf joins the cairns

supplies_trace.prompt: Follow the route on the page and find where the high shelf meets the cairns.

onSuccess.narration: Your finger lands on the exact spot. Brask taps the same place with a claw. "Yes. There."

onFailure.narration: You follow the line off the page and onto the rock. Brask turns the book right way up, gently, and shows you the spot.

ledger_sky.prompt: Use skyward or glide to read both pages from above. The hero with wings helps; choose who leads.
ledger_sky.narration: A griffin can fly up and see a whole ridge at once. A dragonling can glide up on a warm breath of wind. From the sky, the two drawings fit together like halves of a cracker.

onSuccess.narration: From above, the step in the ridge is as plain as a nose. The flyer lands and points straight at it.

onFailure.narration: A gust bats the flyer around. They land with a crumpled page, but the answer is clear: there is a step in the ridge.

compared.narration: The two pages agree on everything but one thing: a step in the ridge, where the stone has slid sideways since the first snow. "The drawing was right when it was drawn," says Brask slowly. "The mountain changed after." He closes the ledger on his pencil. "That is the first half. Now the cairns. The new page draws three of them in a line, and I need to know that my cairns stand in the same order."

choices.label: Look at the cairns

cairn_order.narration: Brask points at three cairns on the slope, and then at three marks on the page. One cairn leans. One has a flat top. One has two stones side by side, like a pair of shoes. Brask hands each of you a scrap of paper. "The scraps hold clues," he says. "Share them out loud."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then put the cairns in the order of the drawing.
clues: The leaning cairn is at the start of the line.
The twin-stone cairn is at the end.
The flat-topped cairn stands between the other two.

onSuccess.narration: Lean, flat, twin! Brask taps each cairn and nods. "The drawing and the mountain agree," he says.

onFailure.narration: You swap two cairns, and Brask gently swaps them back. "The drawing keeps its order," he says kindly. "Cairns are patient."

onAssisted.narration: You lay the scraps side by side. Lean, flat, twin. The order falls out of them like a ribbon.

pebble.narration: A young griffin comes skidding up the last cairn, hugging a rolled page. Her beak is inked, and so is one wing. "This is Pebble," says Brask. "My apprentice. She draws the new page every season." Pebble's feathers droop. "I drew the ridge in the first snow, and it was whole," she says in a rush. "If it moved, did I draw it wrong? Please, will you help me make the page right?"

choices.label: Help Pebble

pebble_help.narration: Pebble holds out her page in both claws. It has a smudge where a tear fell, and a flap that keeps blowing up. "I need it right for the ridge as it is, not as it was," she says. She is trying very hard not to cry, and she has also scraped her wing on the climb. How will you help?

choices.label: Walk her to the step and show her where it moved
Hold the page flat in the wind while she redraws
Use mend on her scraped wing

pebble_walk.prompt: Lead Pebble along the narrow ledge to the step, without a slip.
pebble_walk.narration: The step in the ridge is a short walk along a narrow ledge. Pebble flaps along behind you and keeps stopping to look at her feet.

onSuccess.narration: She sees the step for herself and gasps. "It is not my mistake," she whispers. "It is the mountain's."

onFailure.narration: Pebble wobbles and you catch her by the page. The ledge is narrower than it looked, but she sees the step from where you stand.

pebble_page.prompt: Hold the page flat in the wind while Pebble draws the step.
pebble_page.narration: A wind keeps trying to carry the page away. You flatten it on a rock with a stone on each corner, and Pebble sharpens her pencil with her beak.

onSuccess.narration: The wind sulks and gives up. Pebble draws the step in three quick strokes.

onFailure.narration: The page flaps and rips a corner. Pebble draws on the torn piece, and the step still comes out clear.

pebble_mend.prompt: Use mend on Pebble's scraped wing. The hero with mend helps; choose who leads.
pebble_mend.narration: A unicorn has a gentle touch that makes a scrape stop stinging. It strokes Pebble's wing once, softly, and she holds very still.

onSuccess.narration: The scrape fades, and Pebble flexes her wing in wonder. "It stopped hurting!" She draws much better when nothing hurts.

onFailure.narration: The sting fades, but she is still shaky. She draws slowly and carefully, with her beak scrunched.

pebble_done.narration: Pebble blows on the ink to dry it. The new page shows the notch and the step, and a very small signature in the corner: Pebble. "It was true when I drew it," she says. "Now it is true again." She hugs the page, and then, quickly, she hugs you. She digs in her satchel and presses a squashed supper bundle into your hands. "I packed too much," she says. "Nervous packing."

choices.label: Learn the page by heart

drawing_memory.narration: Pebble taps the marks of her new page on a flat rock, one after another, the way griffins learn a drawing by heart. "Watch it twice," she says, "and then tap it back. If we all remember the page, we can check it against the mountain without the book."

interaction.cue: Watch Pebble's pattern, then tap it back.

onSuccess.narration: Cairn, step, cairn, notch. Pebble beams. "That is the page," she says, "and now it lives in all our heads."

onFailure.narration: One tap comes out in the wrong place. Pebble taps it again, slowly, and you follow along until it sticks.

onAssisted.narration: Pebble taps it slowly, one mark at a time, and you tap along with her until you have it.

moved.narration: Now the question that matters: will it hold? The moved stone is a slab as big as a barn, leaning against the ridge. A pass is only a pass if it holds a foot. "Test it," says Brask. "Gently. It has been through enough." How will you test the slab?

choices.label: Roll a stone along the slab and listen
Lean on the slab together, all at once
Use brace to lean on the slab for the others
Use smash to shove the slab

test_roll.prompt: Roll a stone along the slab and listen for any hollow place.
test_roll.narration: You pick a round stone, set it on the slab, and let it go. It rolls with a rattle, a click, and a long thoughtful hush. Solid rock sounds one way. Hollow rock sounds another.

onSuccess.narration: The sound is steady all the way along: rattle, rattle, rattle. The slab sits on solid rock.

onFailure.narration: The stone rolls off into the snow, and you hear one hollow thump. You cannot say where it came from.

test_lean.prompt: Everyone lean on the slab together and see whether it shifts.
test_lean.narration: You line up along the slab and put your hands on it. Brask counts. Everyone leans at once, as if trying to push over a very large, very patient cow.

onSuccess.narration: The slab does not budge a hair. It is a mountain, after all.

onFailure.narration: The slab gives a grumble and a tiny shiver. Everyone leaps back. A few pebbles tumble, and then it is quiet again.

test_brace.prompt: Use brace to lean on the slab while the others look for cracks. The hero with brace helps; choose who leads.
test_brace.narration: A thornguard knows how to stand firm. That is what brace is for. One of you plants both feet against the slab and takes the push, while the others look for cracks.

onSuccess.narration: The slab does not budge. The thornguard's feet do not budge either, and neither do the cracks.

onFailure.narration: The slab shivers a little under the push, then settles. It is steady enough, but you hold your breath.

test_smash.prompt: Use smash to shove the slab. The hero with smash helps; choose who leads.
test_smash.narration: A bigfoot can shove enormous things. That is what smash is for. One of you leans on the slab with both hands, while the others watch the ground at its foot.

onSuccess.narration: A mighty shove, and the slab shrugs it off. Not one pebble moves.

onFailure.narration: The shove makes the slab shiver. A few pebbles tumble, and then it settles.

tested.narration: The big slab is steady. It slid once, a long time ago, and has settled like a cat on a cushion. But as you check its north edge, a pebble drops through a gap and falls a long way before you hear it land. "The neck," says Brask quietly. "The narrow bridge of rock at the top of the pass. It is hollow underneath."

choices.label: Measure the whole pass

survey.narration: Brask pulls out a long cord with a knot every few steps. "Now we measure it. Length, width, and any place that would make a goat say no." The pass is long, and the neck is narrow, and the shelf below is a long white road. Where will you start?

choices.label: Stretch the cord along the long shelf
Pace the width at each cairn and count
Use skyward or glide to map the pass from above

survey_shelf.prompt: Everyone take a stretch of the cord and pull it tight along the shelf together.
survey_shelf.narration: The cord is long and stiff with frost. Everyone takes a stretch and walks it out along the shelf, from cairn to cairn, until it sings in the wind like a harp.

onSuccess.narration: The cord hums, taut and true, from one end of the shelf to the other. Brask counts the knots and nods.

onFailure.narration: The cord sags in the middle and trips a boot. You untangle it, stretch it again, and count the knots twice.

survey_pace.prompt: Pace the width at every cairn and keep the count straight.
survey_pace.narration: At each cairn, you pace from the cliff to the edge, counting out loud. Pebble counts too, but she counts in griffin, which has different numbers.

onSuccess.narration: Your counts agree from cairn to cairn. The pass is wide as two goats at the narrowest, and wider elsewhere.

onFailure.narration: You lose count at the fourth cairn, and Pebble gets a different number. Brask averages you both with a smile.

survey_sky.prompt: Use skyward or glide to map the pass from above. The hero with wings helps; choose who leads.
survey_sky.narration: A griffin can see a whole ridge at a glance. A dragonling can glide along it. From above, the pass is a long white ribbon, and the measuring is easy.

onSuccess.narration: From above, the pass is a ribbon with a pinch in it. The flyer lands and draws the whole thing from memory.

onFailure.narration: The wind pushes the flyer sideways, so the map comes out a little bent. Brask straightens it with a ruler.

survey_done.narration: Brask writes the numbers into the margin of the ledger in tiny pencil. "Four hundred steps long. Wide as two goats at its narrowest. One hollow neck." Pebble adds a small drawing of a goat for scale. "A pass is a number and a feeling," says Brask. "This one is a good number." He counts six coins from the aerie's surveying purse into your hands, and gives you an owlfeather clasp for the sharpest eyes. "Fee and badge," he says.

choices.label: Take a breath

rest_tea.narration: Brask lights a tiny stove that hisses like a cat. The tea he makes tastes of pine needles and warm stones. Everyone gets a mug, and Pebble gets a thimble. The wind lowers its voice. From the notch, you can see all the way down the valley. There is still the neck to deal with, but not this minute.

choices.label: Drink your tea and watch the valley
Look at the old pages of the ledger
Share your supper with Brask and Pebble

tea_share.narration: You unwrap the supper and share it three ways. Brask gets the cheese, Pebble gets the bread, and the wind gets the crumbs. Pebble is so pleased that she unties a lace from her satchel. "It makes your feet quick," she says. "Mine are quick enough. Mostly." Far below, a line of tiny dots moves along the valley. "Herders," says Brask. "They will want to know this path is real. Let us finish."

choices.label: Finish the job

tea_x.narration: The tea is terrible and wonderful. Far below, a line of tiny dots moves along the valley. "Herders," says Pebble, squinting. "With the herd. They will want to know if this path is real before they trust it with their goats." Brask nods slowly. "Then we had better finish."

choices.label: Finish the job

pages_x.narration: The old pages smell of dust and pencil. Each one shows a pass. Some are crossed out with one neat line. "Closed," says Brask. "Closed. Closed." A few have a tiny star beside them. "Opened. Every road in this book was new once," he says, "even the oldest. Someone had to walk it and write it down." He taps the blank page. "Today that is you."

choices.label: Finish the job

gust.narration: A gust screams over the notch and rips at the ledger. Loose pages leap into the air, flapping like startled birds. "My pages!" cries Pebble. "The new page!" Paper tumbles toward the edge. What do you do?

choices.label: Everyone grab for the flying pages
Throw yourselves on the ledger and hold it shut
Use leap to catch pages in mid-air

gust_grab.prompt: Everyone grab at the flying pages before they reach the edge.
gust_grab.narration: Pages fly everywhere. You snatch at them with both hands, and everybody becomes a very bad flock of birds.

onSuccess.narration: A lot of grabbing and a lot of laughing. When it is over, every page is back in the ledger, a little crumpled.

onFailure.narration: You catch most of them. One page sails over the edge, fluttering down the valley like a lazy gull.

gust_cover.prompt: Hold the ledger shut against the wind.
gust_cover.narration: You fling yourselves on the ledger and hold it shut with your arms. The wind tugs at your sleeves and tries to steal a hat.

onSuccess.narration: The wind gives up and goes to bother someone else. Every page is safe.

onFailure.narration: The wind finds a corner and tugs. One page escapes and flaps away over the valley.

gust_leap.prompt: Use leap to catch pages in mid-air. The hero with leap helps; choose who leads.
gust_leap.narration: A manticore can bound very high and land very softly. The pages are flying, and a bound is a fine way to meet them.

onSuccess.narration: A bound, a twist, a snatch! The pages come down into your arms like tired birds.

onFailure.narration: You catch most of the pages in one bound. One slips away over the valley.

pages_back.narration: Every page is back in the ledger. Pebble hugs the new one and says, "Safe, safe, safe." Brask smooths the corners with his claw. "Now. The herd's supplies," he says, tapping the margin. "If the herders come this way, where can sacks wait out the weather?"

choices.label: Look for a dry place

variants.text: One page is gone, sailing down the valley. It was an old one, a pass long closed, and Brask only sighs. "Perhaps it will teach someone something," he says. Pebble hugs the new page tight. "Now. The herd's supplies," he says, tapping the margin. "If the herders come this way, where can sacks wait out the weather?"

shelter.narration: Along the dry shelf above the flooded route, the cliff leans out in overhangs, and the snow piles into deep banks. A sack of grain wants somewhere dry, out of the wind, and away from nibbling mouths. Where will you look?

choices.label: Check the overhangs for drips and dry rock
Dig a hollow in the deep snowbank
Use leap to reach the high overhang
Buy a waxed sack-cover from Brask for 3 coins

shelter_drip.prompt: Read the overhangs and find the driest one.
shelter_drip.narration: You walk the shelf and look at the underside of each overhang. Drips mean wet. Dust means dry. One nook is so dry that a spider has hung up a tiny sign that says CLOSED.

onSuccess.narration: You find a deep, dry nook, out of the wind, with a floor of clean grit.

onFailure.narration: The first nook drips on your head. The second leaks on your boots. The third is dry enough, but only just.

shelter_dig.prompt: Dig a snow hollow deep enough to hide a stack of sacks.
shelter_dig.narration: A snowbank leans against the cliff, deep and old. Snow makes a fine roof if you dig it right. You scoop with your hands and a flat stone.

onSuccess.narration: The hollow is deep and tidy, with a snow roof as smooth as an egg.

onFailure.narration: The roof sags and drops a cold lump on your neck. You prop it with a stick, and the hollow is small but sound.

shelter_leap.prompt: Use leap to reach the high overhang. The hero with leap helps; choose who leads.
shelter_leap.narration: A manticore can reach a high ledge in a single bound. Up there is an overhang that no goat could climb and no snow could reach.

onSuccess.narration: One bound, and you are up on the ledge. It is dry, deep and perfectly sack-shaped.

onFailure.narration: The bound lands short, and you scrabble up the last bit. The ledge is dry, though, and sack-shaped.

shelter_cover.prompt: Stretch the waxed cover over a nook and pin it down against the wind.
shelter_cover.narration: Brask keeps waxed covers in his pack for the aerie's sacks, and he sells one for a few coins. It is stiff and shiny and smells of candles.

onSuccess.narration: The cover snaps tight over the nook like a drum. Not a drop of weather will get in.

onFailure.narration: The wind grabs a corner and flaps it. You pin it with rocks, and it holds well enough.

shelter_found.narration: Brask draws a little roof on the ledger map and writes "supplies" under it. "Herders come from the glacier side," he says. "A sack left here is a sack saved." Pebble draws a tiny goat under the roof, for luck. "Only one place left to settle," says Brask, and he looks up the pass toward the neck.

choices.label: Go to the neck

neck.narration: The neck is a narrow bridge of rock at the top of the pass. Below it is a gap you could drop a house into. The cairns cross it. Travelers will cross it, and they will want to know how. How will you check the neck?

choices.label: Tie a rope to the last cairn and cross on it
Tap along the neck with a staff and listen

neck_rope.prompt: Cross the neck one at a time on the rope, keeping to the middle.
neck_rope.narration: You tie the rope to the last cairn and tug it hard. One by one you cross the neck, with the rope tight in your fists. Below, the gap yawns as wide as a sleepy giant.

onSuccess.narration: You cross and come back without a pebble falling. The neck holds, if you keep to the middle.

onFailure.narration: A stone slips under a foot. The rope holds, and so do you, but the stone falls for a very long time.

neck_tap.prompt: Tap along the neck with a staff and find where the rock is solid.
neck_tap.narration: A staff tapped on rock tells you a lot. Solid rock says tock. Hollow rock says donk. You walk the edge and listen: tock, tock, donk, tock.

onSuccess.narration: You find the solid line down the middle. It is exactly as wide as one goat, which is exactly as wide as it needs to be.

onFailure.narration: The taps all sound the same to you. Brask taps it again, finds the safe line, and shows you.

neck_done.narration: The safe way over the neck runs down the middle, one traveler wide. Brask draws it as a thin dotted line. "A goat could walk it," he says. "A goat should walk it on a rope." He holds the pencil over the page and looks at you. "Now comes the part only the ledger can do: saying what it is."

choices.label: Decide what to write

mark.narration: Brask holds his pencil over a clean page. "There are three ways to write it, and each is true. A ledger is a promise to the next traveler, so choose with care." Pebble holds her breath. What goes on the page?

choices.label: Write it down as an open pass
Write it down as a pass with a warning at the neck
Write it down as unsettled, closed until it weathers a storm

mark_open.narration: Brask writes OPEN in big, careful letters and underlines it twice. "The herd will be glad," he says, a little too quickly. Pebble clears her throat. "And the neck?" Brask looks at the neck for a long moment. "The neck will have to be careful by itself," he says. "Let us at least put up a good cairn."

choices.label: Raise the last cairn

mark_warn.narration: Brask writes OPEN, WITH CARE, and draws a small hat on the neck, which is how griffins mark a place that needs respect. "Travelers read warnings," he says. "Mostly." Pebble copies the little hat onto her page, very neatly. "And a cairn to go with it," he adds. "A good tall one."

choices.label: Raise the last cairn

mark_closed.narration: Brask writes UNSETTLED in his smallest letters. "The ridge moved once," he says. "I will not send a herd over a thing that might move twice." It is a careful answer, and a bit of a sad one. But a page can be opened later, and a broken step is harder to mend. "We will still raise the cairn," he adds. "A closed road deserves a good marker."

choices.label: Raise the last cairn

capstone.narration: The last cairn goes up at the neck. Its capstone is a heavy flat rock, wide as a table. A cairn this tall wobbles when it is climbed, so it needs one set of hands to hold it and one set to lift. Brask counts to three, then four, because he counted wrong.

interaction.cue: Hold the cairn steady while your friend lifts the capstone.

onSuccess.narration: The capstone settles with a click, and its flat top points down the safe line.

onFailure.narration: The capstone lands crooked. Brask taps it straight with his pencil, and it points the right way.

onAssisted.narration: You wedge a stone under the cairn, and the capstone slides on easily.

capstone_done.narration: The last cairn stands at the neck, tall and neat, and the wind goes around it with a respectful whistle. Pebble holds up one small stone. "The top is where a little stone belongs," she says. "You do it. Brask says anyone who sees it will know someone cared." She also hands you a brass whistle from her satchel. "A griffin signal whistle," she says. "One loud note. Keep it for a moment that needs one."

choices.label: Take the little stone

variants.text: Brask ties a tiny warning flag to it, shaped like a hat.
Brask ties a plain white ribbon to it, to say that the road is resting.

last_stone.narration: The little stone sits in your palm. The top of the capstone has a scratch in the middle, made by Brask's claw. The wind is making the stone want to wander.

interaction.cue: Tap when the stone is over the middle scratch.

onSuccess.narration: Click! The little stone lands right in the middle. Brask tips his head the way griffins do when they are moved.

onFailure.narration: The stone rolls off the edge. Pebble catches it and sets it on top herself. "Practice," she says, kindly.

onAssisted.narration: Pebble steadies your hand, and the little stone settles on top with a click.

signal.narration: Brask lifts his signal flag toward the distant island. "Our neighbors across the sky want to hear what we found," he says. "The flags are a slow talker's tongue, but they carry. What shall we tell them?"

choices.label: Tell them the Cairnstep is real and the ridge moved
Ask whether their own routes have moved too
Blow the brave whistle to catch their eye first

signal_wave.prompt: Wave the signal flags big and slow, in the right order.
signal_wave.narration: Brask hands you a flag on a stick. Big wave, little wave, circle, pause. It is like a dance with a very strict teacher. Across the sky, a tiny figure waits with a flag of its own.

onSuccess.narration: Big wave, little wave, circle, pause. You do it so well that Brask whispers, "Oh, nicely done."

onFailure.narration: You get the circle and the pause backward. Brask quietly fixes it for you, flag by flag.

signal_whistle.prompt: Blow the whistle, then wave the news big and slow.
signal_whistle.narration: Pebble's whistle is small and brass and very loud. You take a deep breath, point it at the distant island, and blow.

onSuccess.narration: The whistle cuts across the sky like a thrown spoon. A tiny figure on the island jumps and waves back at once.

onFailure.narration: The whistle squeaks. Across the sky, a tiny figure waves politely, and you wave the news anyway.

signal_back.narration: Across the gulf of air, the flags answer. Brask reads them aloud, slowly. "They say thank you. They say the ridge is not the only thing that moved. Their old landing route now points into empty sky." He lowers the flag. "I would like to know how that happened, and so would they."

choices.label: Hear what Brask suggests

variants.text: Across the gulf of air, the flags answer. Brask reads them aloud, slowly. "They say yes. They say their old landing route now points into empty sky." He lowers the flag. "I would like to know how that happened, and so would they."

message.narration: Brask closes the ledger and ties it with a ribbon. The pass shines below in the last light, a ribbon of stones with a safe line down its middle. "You walked it," he says. "That makes it a pass. Now it is in the book." He looks at the island and its flags. "Our neighbors have trouble with their routes too. There are more places to investigate after this first visit. We can bring your whole party across to ask them, if you like."

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
